q: 1. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to ...........
explain: Better grading of aggregate reduces voids and internal friction, thereby increasing the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 2. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to ...........
explain: As the time of transit increases, concrete loses moisture due to evaporation and hydration, causing workability to decrease.

q: 3. Air entrainment in the concrete increases ...........
explain: Air entraining agents create minute air bubbles that act like ball bearings, significantly increasing the workability of the mix.

q: 4. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about ...........
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength over time due to slow hydration; after one year, it is typically 20-25% stronger than at 28 days.

q: 5. The surface width of cracks shall not generally exceed ...........
explain: For members under moderate exposure conditions, the maximum crack width is limited to 0.3 mm to ensure durability.

q: 6. As per I.S.: 456-1978, the pH value of water shall be ...........
explain: Water used for mixing and curing concrete must be clean and have a pH value not less than 6 to avoid acidic attack on the concrete.

q: 7. Working loads may be defined as ...........
options: maximum loads consisting of dead and live loads
a set of critical loads in service conditions
all loads that occur during service conditions
a set of maximum loads for which no failure will occur
explain: Working loads (service loads) are the actual loads expected to occur on the structure during its normal life.

q: 8. The maintenance cost of concrete structures is ...........
options: as much as for timber structures
explain: Unlike steel or timber, concrete does not rust or rot easily, making its long-term maintenance costs very low.

q: 9. The probability that the actual strength of the material is more than its characteristic strength is ...........
explain: Characteristic strength is defined as the value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall, meaning 95% are above it.

q: 10. In the limit state design, the strength of concrete as well as the strength of steel is taken to be a random variable that follows ...........
explain: Structural engineering codes assume a Normal (Gaussian) distribution for the frequency of material strength results.

q: 11. The chances for the actual strength of concrete to be less than its characteristic strength are ...........
explain: By definition, the characteristic strength (fck) allows for a 5% probability of failure (strength being lower than fck).

q: 12. In terms of the mean load Fm and the standard deviation of the load Fs, the characteristic load Fk is given by ...........
explain: Characteristic load is the value that has a 95% probability of not being exceeded during the life of the structure.

q: 13. In limit state design, the relationship between stress strain distribution in concrete is assumed to be ...........
explain: IS:456 assumes a stress-strain curve for concrete that is parabolic up to 0.002 strain and constant thereafter up to 0.0035 strain.

q: 14. Concrete fails at a strain of ...........
explain: In the Limit State of collapse (flexure), the maximum strain in concrete at the outermost compression fiber is assumed to be 0.0035.

q: 15. The moment of resistance factor Ru is given as ...........
explain: The Moment of Resistance (Mu) is calculated as $M_u = R_u \cdot b \cdot d^2$, making $R_u = M_u / (b \cdot d^2)$.

q: 16. For a fixed beam of span l carrying uniformly distributed load the bending moment at the critical section is given by ...........
explain: For a fixed-ended beam with UDL, the maximum bending moment occurs at the supports (fixed ends) and is equal to $wl^2/12$.

q: 17. The moment of resistance factor Ru, lim when Fe415 steel is used, is given by ...........
explain: For Fe415 steel, the limiting moment of resistance factor is $0.138 \cdot f_{ck}$ based on the strain limit in steel.

q: 18. The assessed surface width of crack should not generally exceed ...........
explain: While 0.3mm is allowed for mild exposure, many design specifications (especially in older or more stringent codes) target 0.2mm for better durability.

q: 19. Working stress design assumes ...........
explain: The Working Stress Method is based on the elastic theory, assuming that both steel and concrete behave linearly and elastically under service loads.

q: 20. Working stress design assumes ...........
options: partial recovery of deflections caused during some load condition
full recovery of deflections caused during some load conditions
partial recovery of deflections caused in all types of load conditions
full recovery of deflections caused in all types of load conditions
explain: Because it assumes perfect elasticity, the WSM implies that when the load is removed, the structure returns to its original shape (full recovery).

q: 21. The approximate allowable stress in bending compression in reinforced concrete is ...........
explain: In WSM, the permissible stress in bending compression (sigma_cbc) is roughly $f_{ck}/3$, which is approximately $0.33 \cdot f_{ck}$.

q: 22. In a singly reinforced beam, the effective depth is measured from its compression edge to ...........
explain: Effective depth 'd' is the distance from the extreme compression fiber to the center of gravity of the tensile reinforcement.

q: 23. If d and n are the effective depth and depth of the neutral axis respectively of a singly reinforced beam, the lever arm of the beam is ...........
explain: Lever arm is the distance between the total compressive force (acting at n/3 from the top) and the tensile force: $z = d - n/3$.

q: 24. By over-reinforcing a beam, the moment resistance can be increased not more than ............
explain: According to limit state design principles, over-reinforcing a section beyond the balanced condition provides diminishing returns in moment capacity, generally capped around 25% due to the brittle nature of concrete failure.

q: 25. The compression force $C_u$ resisted by the concrete above neutral axis will be acting at a distance ............ from the extreme compression fibre.
explain: In the Limit State Method parabolic stress block, the centroid of the compressive force is located at $0.416 x_u$ (approximately $3/7 x_u$) from the extreme compression fiber.

q: 26. In a singly reinforced concrete beam, if the load is very small ............
options: only steel bars will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist compression
explain: At very low loads (uncracked stage), the concrete remains intact and both the concrete and steel contribute to resisting tensile stresses.

q: 27. In a singly reinforced concrete beam, as the load increases ............
options: only steel bars will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist compression
explain: Once the tensile stress exceeds the modulus of rupture of concrete, the concrete cracks. Beyond this point, only the steel bars are assumed to resist the total tensile force.

q: 28. In a beam section, if the steel reinforcement is of such a magnitude that the permissible stresses in concrete and steel are developed simultaneously, the section is known as ............
explain: A section where both materials reach their maximum allowable stresses at the same time is variously referred to as a balanced, critical, or economical section.

q: 29. The moment of resistance of an under-reinforced section is computed on the basis of ............
explain: Since steel reaches its permissible limit first in an under-reinforced section, the moment of resistance is governed by the steel capacity ($M = A_st \cdot \sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d$).

q: 30. The neutral axis of an over-reinforced section falls ............
explain: Because there is more steel than required for a balanced section, the neutral axis must shift downward (below the critical N.A.) to provide a larger compression area to balance the tension.

q: 31. The neutral axis in T-beam section falls
explain: Depending on the reinforcement area and flange dimensions, the neutral axis can either lie within the slab (flange) or extend down into the rib.

q: 32. The width of the flange of T-beam should be less than
options: one-third of the effective span of the T-beam
distance between the centres of T-beam
breadth of the rib plus twelve times the thickness of the slab
explain: The effective width of a T-beam flange is limited to the minimum of several factors (span/6 + bw + 6df, or center-to-center distance) to account for shear lag.

q: 33. For the design of a simply supported T-beam the ratio of the effective span to the overall depth the beam is limited to
explain: For span/depth ratios regarding deflection control (IS 456), the value for a simply supported beam is generally taken as 20.

q: 34. The maximum strain in the tension reinforcement at failure shall not be less than
explain: Per Limit State Method (IS 456), the minimum strain in steel at failure to ensure ductility is (0.87fy / Es) + 0.002. Note: 0.87 is 1/1.15.

q: 35. The ratio of the compressive strength of concrete is structure to the characteristic strength of concrete in cube is equal to
explain: Because of size and shape differences between a test cube and the actual structure, the design compressive strength of concrete in the structure is taken as 0.67 times the cube strength (fck).

q: 36. The shape of the stress-strain curve for compression in concrete is generally taken to be
explain: In the Limit State Method, the stress-strain block is usually assumed to be parabolic up to a strain of 0.002 and rectangular thereafter.

q: 37. The maximum allowable percentage of tension reinforcement in R.C.C. beams is
explain: To prevent congestion and ensure proper concrete placement, IS 456 limits the maximum area of tension reinforcement to 4% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 38. The maximum area of tension reinforcement in beams shall not exceed
explain: Same as Q240; the limit is 4% of the gross area (bD).

q: 39. Concrete is fairly strong in
options: tension but very weak in compression
compression but very weak in tension
explain: Concrete is a brittle material that performs well under compression but has very little tensile strength (roughly 1/10th of its compressive strength).

q: 40. The simple bending equation is applicable to a reinforced concrete beam subjected to a monotonously increasing load when the beam remains in
explain: Simple bending theory (linear elastic) applies best when the section is homogenous and uncracked. Once cracks appear, the section properties change significantly.

q: 41. If the ratio of steel to concrete in a beam is such that maximum strain in both materials reach simultaneously, the beam is referred to as
explain: A balanced section is a theoretical design where the concrete reaches its maximum allowable compressive strain at the exact same time the steel reaches its yield strain.

q: 42. When strains in compression zone of the concrete of a loaded singly reinforced beam, cause crushing of concrete, the failure is known as
explain: Primary compression failure occurs in over-reinforced sections where concrete reaches its limit before the steel yields.

q: 43. The capacity of beam is determined by the load which causes
explain: In standard under-reinforced design, the beam's capacity is reached when the steel yields (ultimate limit state).

q: 44. For cantilever beams and slabs, the basic value of span to effective depth ratio is
explain: The code provides basic L/d ratios for deflection control: 7 for cantilevers, 20 for simply supported, and 26 for continuous.

q: 45. For the simply supported beams and slabs the basic value of span to effective depth ratio is
explain: As per IS 456, the basic span-to-effective-depth ratio for simply supported members is 20.

q: 46. The minimum factor of safety against sliding for a retaining wall is
explain: The minimum factor of safety against sliding is 1.5, often increased if soil conditions are poor.

q: 47. The structural analysis used in the ultimate strength design of R.C.C. structure is
explain: Even though we design for ultimate strength, the distribution of forces is still usually based on linear elastic analysis.

q: 48. For a balanced design, according to I.S. : 456, the maximum depth of concrete stress block in R.C.C. beams should be
explain: For Fe250 steel, the limiting neutral axis depth (Xu,max) is 0.53d.

q: 49. Prestressing in concrete beams is usually obtained by
explain: Most prestressed concrete involves internal prestressing, where tendons are placed within the concrete section (either pre-tensioned or post-tensioned in ducts).

q: 50. The length of a reinforced concrete pile is taken as ............ the length embedded in firm stratum.
explain: In certain design simplified assumptions, the effective length of the pile is taken as half of the total length if the soil provides significant lateral restraint.
